یہ قافلہ شبیر کی مقتل سے گزرنا

بے آسرا سیدانیاں اور میل ہزاروں
اب تک بھی یتیموں کا کوئی زخم نہ بھرنا

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/abbas-ka-maidan.md')
original = p.read_bytes()
before, rest = original.decode().split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)
roman, after = rest.split('# source_id:', 1)
changes = {
    'Ghazi ki shahadat': 'Ghaazi ki shahaadat',
    'ghazi': 'Ghaazi',
    'zainab': 'Zainab',
    'maidaṅ': 'maidaaṅ',
    'meiṅ': 'mein',
    'Haathoṅ mei rasan': 'Haathoṅ mein rasan',
    'Qaimon': 'Khaimoṅ',
    'yatimoṅ': 'yatimoṅ',
    'sunani jo sunayi': 'sunaani jo sunaai',
    'dhunda': 'dhunda',
    'tamachoṅ': 'tamaanchoṅ',
    'sakina': 'Sakina',
    'shaam e gharibaṅ': 'shaam-e-gharibaaṅ',
    'khafela shabbir': 'qaafila Shabbir',
    'galiyoiṅ mein phirana': 'galiyoṅ mein phirna',
    'eid manana': 'Eid manaana',
    'Ujre huwoṅ': 'Ujre huoṅ',
    'ka sawarna': 'ka sanwarna',
    'tamil hazaroṅ': 'taamil hazaaroṅ',
    'Beaasra saydaniyaṅ aur mil hazaroṅ': 'Beaasra sayyidaaniyaaṅ aur mail hazaaroṅ',
    'aankheiṅ': 'aankheṅ',
    'Maruf kabhi shaukat o farhan': 'Maaruf kabhi Shaukat o Farhaan',
    'meherban': 'meherbaan',
    'nauhe': 'nohe',
}
for old, new in changes.items():
    assert old in roman, old
    roman = roman.replace(old, new)
source = after.split('\\n---\\n\\n', 1)[1]
source_lines = source.splitlines()
roman_lines = [line[2:] for line in roman.splitlines()]
assert len(source_lines) == len(roman_lines)
assert (source_lines[0], roman_lines[0]) == ('۱', '1')
assert all(c.isascii() or c in 'ṅṄ' for c in roman)
result = (before + 'romanLyrics: |-\\n' + roman + '# source_id:' + after).encode()
assert result.split(b'# source_id:', 1)[1] == original.split(b'# source_id:', 1)[1]
p.write_bytes(result)
print(f'Checked {len(roman_lines) - 1} verse lines. Urdu and metadata preserved.')
PY"

item.text:
Audited all 41 Roman verses in [abbas-ka-maidan.md](src/data/lyrics/abbas-ka-maidan.md) against the Urdu. Corrected readings including `Khaimoṅ`, `qaafila`, `galiyoṅ mein phirna`, and `sanwarna`, and standardized nasal endings and name capitalization.

The Urdu text, stanza structure, and metadata were preserved. The Roman reading `mail` for میل remains unverified by recitation.
